script: [serious] At 8:43 in the morning on July 2nd, 1937, Amelia Earhart's voice came over the radio for the last time: We are on the line, 157, 337. She and her navigator, Fred Noonan, were flying a Lockheed Electra toward Howland Island, a speck of land in the middle of the Pacific. They never arrived. She had already radioed that they must be close, but couldn't see the island, and fuel was running low. So what happened? One: they ran out of fuel and sank. That's the official answer. But a deep-sea sonar search of six hundred and thirty square miles found nothing. Two: they landed on Nikumaroro, an empty reef about 350 nautical miles away. In 1940, a British colonial officer found thirteen bones there, the remains of a shoe, and a sextant box. The bones were later lost. Three: they were captured by Japan. No record has ever proven it. Which do you believe? Send this to someone who loves an unsolved case. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number fourteen. A new file every day.
